points.description: Names all three classes correctly: unconfirmed connectionless, confirmed connectionless, connection-oriented (all three required, with correct terms).
points.partial_credit: Two of the three named correctly gives half.

points.description: Unconfirmed connectionless: no acknowledgement, data loss possible, no flow control, no connect/disconnect (must state no ACK and loss possible, plus at least no connection setup).
points.partial_credit: No ACK and loss of data stated, but no mention of flow control/connection setup, gives half.

points.description: Confirmed connectionless: uses ACK, no loss of data but timeout and retransmission can cause duplicates and sequencing errors, no flow control, no connect/disconnect.
points.partial_credit: ACK and no loss stated but duplicates/sequence errors omitted (or the reverse) gives half.

points.description: Connection-oriented: no data loss, no duplication, no sequencing errors; three-phase communication (connect, data transfer, disconnect) with flow control.
points.partial_credit: Reliability (no loss/duplicates/sequence errors) stated, but three phases or flow control missing, gives half.

rubric.notes: Harsh: each class's differences must be stated precisely with the correct terms (ACK, flow control, connect/disconnect, duplicates/sequencing errors). Vague statements such as 'one is more reliable' earn nothing. A wrong detail (e.g. saying confirmed connectionless has flow control or connection setup) cancels that point.
